item.title: Cyprus leaders agree to open new border crossings and future talks
item.description:
By Yiannis Kourtoglou

NICOSIA, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot leaders agreed on Monday to open two new border crossings, coordinate on emergency responses and share archival materials as part of a UN-backed effort to resume peace talks after nearly a decade of deadlock.

That brought the number of open crossings on the divided Mediterranean island to 11, according to media in Cyprus.

item.title: French officials accuse Iran of being behind refrigerator hacks
item.description:
By Raphael Satter and Gabriel Stargardter

PARIS, Nov 9 (Reuters) - French officials on Monday accused Iran's Revolutionary Guards of responsibility for the cyberattacks that knocked outcommercial refrigerators and freezers across France last month, saying there would be consequences for Iran.

item.title: Syria, Jordan seek to mend ties after deadly airstrikes, sign cooperation deals
item.description:
DAMASCUS, Nov 9 - The foreign ministers of Syria and Jordan met in Damascus on Monday for the first time since Jordanian airstrikes killed civilians in southern Syria last month, announcing a joint investigation into the incident and signing 11 new cooperation agreements.

Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani said Jordan had shown understanding and openness towards resolving the incident in Deraa province, adding that the two countries had set up a joint security and technical committee to investigate the circumstances of the airstrikes.

item.title: Four killed in Gaza after sand embankment collapses on to tents
item.description:
By Nidal al-Mughrabi and Mahmoud Issa

CAIRO/GAZA, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Torrential rain in Gaza caused a sand embankment to collapse on to tents, killing a woman and three small children in an incident that highlighted the danger facing hundreds of thousands of displaced Palestinians as the rainy winter season sets in.

item.title: Trump to meet Iran war mediator Qatar, no imminent deal seen to end the war
item.description:
By Yomna Ehab and Alexander Cornwell

CAIRO/ABU DHABI, Nov 9 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump will meet the prime minister of key mediator Qatar on Monday as efforts to end the Iran war ramp up following last week's midterm elections, though senior US and Gulf officials cast doubt on the chances of an imminent deal.

More than eight months into the conflict he launched alongside Israel on February 28, Trump has played down the likelihood of major warfare restarting soon but remains unwilling to accept an existing Iranian truce plan.

item.title: Eisenkot's strange bedfellow options to lead Israel
item.description:
Israel's former army chief Gadi Eisenkot has a matter of weeks to form a government, despite not having won a clear majority in the new parliament.

Eisenkot has a number of options, although none look ideal for him, to reach the magic number of 61 in the 120-member parliament.

President Isaac Herzog on Sunday gave Eisenkot the mandate to try to form a government, setting the clock at 28 days for him to come up with the 61 votes, although Herzog could give him a 14-day extension.

item.title: Iran defends two-day proposal for peace talks after US rejects conditions
item.description:
DUBAI, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Iran defended a proposal on Monday to restart peace talks in as few as two days as the most reasonable offer on the table, after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called some of Iran's conditions "outrageous and ridiculous".

"Is it unreasonable that Iran demands that US illegal sanctions and its naval blockade must be lifted before negotiations start and that the war should end on all fronts?" Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei told a weekly press conference in response to Rubio's remarks.

item.title: China seeks to build ties with Iran
item.description:
HONG KONG, Nov 9 (Reuters) - China is willing to pursue stronger ties with Iran, China's special envoy to the Middle East Zhai Jun said in talks with Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council.

Zhai met Kani in Iran, according to a readout from China's foreign ministry on Monday. He is visiting Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month, as China steps up efforts to ease tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: This year set to be one of four hottest on record, UN report says
item.description:
GENEVA, Nov 9 (Reuters) - This year is on track to be one of the four hottest on record, driven by a powerful ElNiño and perpetuating a warming streak of more than a decade, a UNreport showed on Monday.

• Countries are preparing tomeet in Turkey ​from November 9 to 20 for the next round of climate talks and the World Meteorological Organization "State of the Climate"report provides the latest available data to inform their discussions.

item.title: UAE's Gargash warns of prolonged regional uncertainty, says US-Iran settlement appears difficult
item.description:
By Alexander Cornwell

ABU DHABI, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Senior Emirati official Anwar Gargash warned on Monday that the region could face a prolonged period of uncertainty, saying a comprehensive political settlement between the United States and Iran to end the more than eight-month war appeared to be difficult.

item.title: Exclusive-Covert Russian network exploited French riots on social media, EU report says
item.description:
By Antoni Slodkowski and John Irish

NEW YORK/PARIS, Nov 9 (Reuters) - A covert Russian network sought to exploit last month's riots in France by using social media to blame the unrest on uncontrolled immigration and portray the government as having lost control, according to an internal EU assessment seen by Reuters.
